summary: Story Mode turns your Dev Clock time into an adventure map, and every new version now opens with a short animated trailer.
notes: Story Mode: Rex walks a trail of 12 places. Every Dev Clock session moves Rex further and unlocks new places, from Hatchling Hollow to The Summit of Rex at 100 hours.
changes: Story Mode: Rex walks a trail of 12 places. Every Dev Clock session moves Rex further and unlocks new places, from Hatchling Hollow to The Summit of Rex at 100 hours.
Update trailer: the first time you open a newer version, Rex waves, the version name flies in and the changes roll by like movie credits. Skip it any time.
Places you reach stay reached, and Rex tells you when you arrive somewhere new. Progress is only your real Dev Clock time.
The trailer respects reduce motion, never plays on a brand-new install, and can be turned off or replayed in Settings → App & Updates.
Updates still only install when you press Install.

history.summary: Story Mode turns your Dev Clock time into an adventure map, and every new version now opens with a short animated trailer.

items.text: Story Mode: Rex walks a trail of 12 places. Every Dev Clock session moves Rex further and unlocks new places, from Hatchling Hollow to The Summit of Rex at 100 hours.
Update trailer: the first time you open a newer version, Rex waves, the version name flies in and the changes roll by like movie credits. Skip it any time.
Places you reach stay reached, and Rex tells you when you arrive somewhere new. Progress is only your real Dev Clock time.
The trailer respects reduce motion, never plays on a brand-new install, and can be turned off or replayed in Settings → App & Updates.
Updates still only install when you press Install.

history.summary: A friendly first visit: Rex asks what to call you, then walks you through your first Discord webhook.

items.text: A new install opens a welcome window that asks what Rex should call you and saves it to your profile.
Guided first webhook: where to find the link in Discord, a plain-words check of what you paste, then save and send a test message with a clear result.
Both steps can be skipped. If you skip, or you already use Rex, a small card on Home offers them with a Not now button. You can also run them from the command palette.
The Update Log no longer shows up underneath every other page after you have opened it once.
The tour is now offered at the end of the welcome instead of starting on top of it.
Updates still only install when you press Install.

history.summary: The Home update card shows what is new before you install, you can ask Rex to remind you later, and the Update Log is steadier on phones.

items.text: Home shows the new version with its name, a short summary and the first few changes. Install and Read all notes are right there.
Remind me later: hide the update card and the red dot for 1 hour, 4 hours or until tomorrow morning. Show it now brings it back.
The install window has a Remind me later button too. It hides the update card for an hour and installs nothing.
The Update Log is lighter on phones: release details are built only when you open a card, a search opens at most three cards, and one failed draw can no longer take the page down.
If the phone closed the page while the Update Log was drawing, the next visit opens a light view with fewer releases and a button to switch back.
Opening the Update Log checks for an announcement at most once a minute instead of every time.
A reminder only hides the card on this device. Nothing is installed until you press Install, and a newer version brings the card back.

history.summary: A clearer, nicer install window with both version names, what is new and what will happen.

items.text: The install window shows the version you have and the one you are getting, with their names, a short list of what is new and three plain steps.
The restore point option is now a proper switch with a short explanation instead of a loose checkbox.
Updates still only install when you press Install.

history.summary: A tiny release made to try a scheduled release: it was uploaded early and held back until the countdown reached zero.

items.text: No new features. This release exists to test scheduled releases from start to finish: upload early, countdown, then the update appears at zero.
Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Scheduled releases: an update can be uploaded early and held back until a set time, with a countdown.

items.text: Scheduled releases. A release can now carry a release time. Rex shows a live countdown, does not offer the update until the time arrives, and then finds it by itself so you can press Update Now. The new tools/release-at.sh sets the time and the countdown in one step.
When the countdown reaches zero, Rex keeps checking about once a minute (up to 8 times) until the update shows up, and the countdown card says when the update is ready.
It uses each device’s own clock, so a device with a wrong clock may see the update early or late. Older versions of Rex do not hold updates back. Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Countdown fixes: it now notices a new announcement while Rex is open, and the Update Log says why when there is no countdown.

items.text: The next-update countdown only looked for an announcement when Rex opened, so an announcement made while Rex was already open (or just after you opened it) did not show up. Rex now looks again about every 3 minutes while it is open, when you come back to the tab, and whenever you press Check for Updates.

Announcement times written like “2026-10-18 12:00” are now understood on every browser (Safari used to reject that format, so no countdown appeared). Times with a zone, such as ...Z or -04:00, still work.

The Update Log now has a small status line that says what Rex knows about the next update: nothing announced, could not reach the website, the file is not valid, you already have that version, or the time has passed. It has a Check now button.
Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: A small test release for the next-update countdown.

items.text: The Update Center now shows when the version you are running was released, next to its number.

When the next-update countdown reaches zero, Rex now does one ordinary update check by itself (only if automatic update checks are on), so the new version shows up in the Update Center without you pressing Check. It still never installs anything.
This release was announced ahead of time, so Home and the Update Log counted down to it. Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: A much nicer Update Log: a featured latest release, real totals, filters with counts, months, and collapsible release cards.

items.text: The Update Log has a new look. The newest release sits at the top in a featured card with its highlights, the totals (releases, new features, improvements, fixes) are counted from the real release history, and releases are grouped by month.

Each release is a compact card with its icon, version and name, date, a small count of what changed, and a one-line summary. Tap a card to open the full list, grouped as New, Improved, Fixed and Removed. Expand all / Collapse all opens or closes every card.

Search now finds words in the summary, the version number and the release name, highlights what it found, and opens the matching cards for you. The type filters show how many changes match, and a friendly empty state appears when nothing does.
“Since my last visit” shows how many releases you have not opened yet. A brand-new visitor is no longer shown every old release as NEW.

Lighter on phones: no banner picture on every card, no blur layers, and releases still load 8 at a time with Show older / Show all. Release links (#update-…), the full release page and Update Achievements (now in a collapsible section) all still work.

Next update countdown: when a release time is announced, Home and the Update Log show a live countdown to it, and when the time arrives they say the update is out and point you to the Update Center. Nothing is ever installed for you.
Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Live Event reminders: a banner when an event starts and when one is about to end.

items.text: Live Event reminders: a dismissible banner at the top of Rex when a Live Event has just started (first 24 hours) and when one is about to end (3 hours to 2 days before, your choice). It has an Open button and a Dismiss button, and shows your real collecting progress when the event has a hunt.

Settings → Alerts has a new Live Event reminders card: turn reminders on or off, pick start and/or ending reminders, choose how early “about to end” means, preview a reminder, or bring dismissed ones back.

Reminders use only this device’s clock and only appear while Rex is open. There are no push notifications, servers or tracking. Short events use half their length for “ending soon”, and each reminder shows once until you reset them.

Every update now has a name next to its number, with one name for computers and another for phones. This one is V12.8.1 Max on computers and V12.8.1 Rex on phones. The name shows in the sidebar, Home, Settings, the Update Log and the Update Center.
The reminder settings are included in Full backup & restore. Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Full backup and restore, a first-run tour, and a searchable shortcuts list. All free and all on your device.

items.text: Full backup & restore (Settings → Data): download one file with everything Rex keeps in this browser, grouped into sections you can tick: webhooks, templates and profile; appearance and favorites; Rex Studio; Dev Clock; Live Events progress, rewards and skins; achievements; friends; and other settings. You can leave your webhook URLs out of the file.

Restore checks the file first, shows a preview, and lets you pick which sections to restore. It only writes what is in the file and ticked, never deletes anything else, keeps a safety copy, and has an "Undo last restore" button. Old Rex backup files and restore-point exports can be restored too. Nothing is ever uploaded.

First-run tour: a short spotlight walkthrough of the sidebar, Favorites, search, Live Events, manual updates and shortcuts. It starts by itself only on a brand-new install. Replay it any time from the shortcuts list or the command palette ("Take the tour").
The shortcuts list (press ?) now has a search box, groups, and also lists every command in the Ctrl/⌘+K palette.

Restoring from Rex Backups (Restore Points) could be silently undone: the page’s auto-save wrote the old data back over the restored data when Rex reloaded. It now stops auto-save during a restore, so the restored data stays.
Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Live Events now show up on the Holiday Center calendar.

items.text: Every Live Event appears on the Holiday Calendar: a colored bar on each day it runs, the event’s emoji on its first day, and a "Live Events this month" list under the calendar.
Pick a day to see which events run then, their dates, whether they are live, upcoming or ended, how many items you have found, and a button that opens the event.

A switch under the calendar hides or shows the events (remembered on this device). Event dates follow this device’s clock, like Live Events itself. Holidays, hidden holidays and the calendar export are unchanged, and updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Sixteen funny Live Events, so there is something silly in almost every month, plus a fix for the Rex Insider "See what is coming" button.

items.text: Sixteen funny bonus events: Squirrel Appreciation Day, Groundhog Day, National Pizza Day, National Napping Day, April Fools’ Day, Lost Sock Memorial Day, National Donut Day, World Emoji Day, National Ice Cream Day, International Cat Day, Sneak Zucchini onto a Porch Day, Ask a Silly Question Day, National Taco Day, International Sloth Day, National Sandwich Day and Clean Out Your Refrigerator Day.

Each has hidden collectibles, rewards, a Rex skin and its own effect (also available in the Effect Lab). April Fools’ Day only hides harmless pranks: nothing in the app changes or breaks. Live Events now has 41 events.

In Rex Insider, the "See what is coming" button did nothing because it linked to the page you were already on. It now opens the Coming Soon tab. Announcement links can point at any Insider tab (see the note at the top of js/insider-data.js).

history.summary: Search everything from the command palette, a lighter Update Log for phones, and nine more Live Events.

items.text: Global search: press Ctrl/⌘+K (or open the command palette) and type. Rex now also finds your pages, projects, project tasks, notebook entries, Knowledge Base notes, tasks, workflows, templates, drafts, webhook names and Live Events. Press Enter to open the page and highlight the match.

The Update Log could crash on phones. It used to draw every release (more than 70, each with a gradient banner) in one go. It now shows the newest 8 and a "Show older releases" button, skips the heavy visual effects on small screens, no longer draws itself at start-up, and redraws search results after you pause typing. If drawing ever fails, it shows a "Try again" button instead of crashing.

Nine new Live Events: Lunar New Year, Pi Day, First Day of Spring, Moon Landing Day, National Dog Day, Programmers’ Day, Talk Like a Pirate Day, International Coffee Day and Ada Lovelace Day. Each has hidden collectibles, rewards, a Rex skin and its own effect (also available in the Effect Lab).
Search only reads your saved data and never changes it. Webhook URLs are never searched or shown. Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Live Events dates are now fixed: the Schedule section was removed from Live Events settings.

items.text: Removed the Schedule card (the start and end date editor) from Live Events → Settings. Event dates always use the built-in calendar now.
Any custom dates saved earlier are ignored so events follow the built-in dates. Your saved event progress and rewards are not touched.

history.summary: Achievements 2.0: a Platinum tier, secret achievements, categories, points and levels.

items.text: Every multi-tier achievement now has a fourth Platinum tier, and four new achievements were added: Reward Collector, Wardrobe, Pin Master and Profile Pro.
Six secret achievements stay hidden (with a vague hint) until you earn them, such as Night Owl, Early Bird and Marathon Session. They unlock from your real Dev Clock, Profile and Live Events data.
Points and levels: every tier earns points, and your level and title rise as you collect them. A Next up box shows the goals you are closest to, and Recent unlocks lists your latest badges.

Filter by category (Build, Time, Rex Studio, Safety, Social, Events, Customize, Secrets) and by status. Tier rarity shows difficulty only; Rex has no server, so it never compares you with other people.
Your existing Bronze, Silver and Gold badges and their dates are kept exactly as they were. Nothing was reset, and updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: A better Profile: cleaner header, two-column layout, Profile strength, a Rewards shelf and a workspace summary.

items.text: The header is bigger and cleaner: a taller banner, a larger avatar, your name and status sit clear of the banner, and quick chips show your role, project, region, member-since date and equipped skin.
New Profile strength card shows how complete your profile is (real fields only) with one-tap Add buttons that open Edit Profile.
New Rewards shelf lists the badges and Rex skins you have really earned in Live Events, with an empty state if you have none yet.
New Workspace at a glance shows your real counts of projects, notes, finished tasks, restore points and pinned pages.
Two columns on wide screens, one column on phones. Your saved profile, privacy switches, friends and backups are untouched. Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: Favorites: pin your most-used pages to the top of the sidebar and jump to them with Alt+1 to Alt+8.

items.text: Hover any page in the sidebar and press the small star to pin it. Pinned pages appear in a Favorites group at the top (up to 8). Press the star again to unpin. On a phone the stars are always visible.

Alt+1 to Alt+8 open your first eight favorites (they do nothing while you are typing in a box or a dialog is open). "Pin or unpin this page" is also in the command palette (Ctrl/⌘+K), and the Dashboard Quick links show your favorites first.
Favorites are saved only on this device and never change the pages themselves. Updates still only install when you press Update Now.

history.summary: A full visual refresh: new dark design system, redesigned sidebar and Dashboard, and a new Rex icon.

items.text: New dark, deep-navy look with blue, violet and cyan accents, applied across every page: cards, buttons, forms, dialogs, focus outlines and notifications now share one style. Light mode still works, and your Appearance choices (accent colour, card style, fonts, sidebar mode) are kept.

Redesigned sidebar: a new logo with the version shown, one icon style for every page, collapsible groups (Overview, Create, Rex Studio, News & Events, Monitor & Test, System), a collapse-to-icons button, and a Rex footer. On phones it is still a slide-in menu.

New Dashboard overview with search, cards for your real projects, notes, backups, next event, webhooks and open tasks, quick actions, recent activity and a Rex Insider news preview. Anything with no data shows a friendly empty message instead of made-up numbers.
A new Rex mascot icon for the app, the browser tab and the home-screen icon. An Update Center link in the sidebar opens Settings, App & Updates, and shows a dot when a newer version is published.
The sun/moon button now remembers your choice after a reload. New installs start in dark mode; if you already saved an Appearance choice, it is unchanged.
Updates still only install when you press Update Now. Refreshing, reopening or checking never installs anything, and your saved data was not changed by this release.

history.summary: Rex Insider: a news room inside Project Rex with announcements, coming soon, development notes, release history and event previews.

items.text: New Rex Insider page with five tabs: Featured, Coming Soon, Development, Release History and Event Previews. A small badge on the menu shows announcements you have not read yet.

Release History reads the same Update Log as before (with search). Event Previews shows the next seasonal events with countdowns and a button that opens Holiday Live Events, where you actually take part.

Announcements live in one easy file (js/insider-data.js) and arrive with an app update. Nothing is fetched from the internet and no data is sent anywhere. Rex Insider only saves which announcements you have read.

history.summary: Holiday Live Events: scheduled holiday events with hidden collectibles, achievements, rewards and effects, starting with the Halloween Haunt.

items.text: New Live Events page with 16 events: New Year's Day, Winter Season, Valentine's Day, St. Patrick's Day, Easter, Earth Day, Memorial Day (kept quiet, no games), First Day of Summer, Independence Day, Back-to-School Season, First Day of Fall, Halloween, Thanksgiving and Christmas, plus two bonus days (National Pet Day, National Video Games Day).

Events switch between Upcoming, Live and Archived by themselves using this device's clock, with countdowns and an Upcoming preview. Easter, Thanksgiving and Memorial Day are calculated for any year. No app update is needed for an event that is already in the app. This is not a worldwide live event: it follows your own time zone, and progress stays in this browser.

Halloween Haunt (Oct 24-31 by default): 13 friendly pumpkins hidden at the bottom of pages, a rare Golden Pumpkin, clues, a 4-chapter secret story, a Haunted Portal, a mystery reward and optional ghosts, bats, fog, falling leaves and orange sparks.

The same system powers the others: a 25-day Advent calendar with hidden presents, an Easter egg hunt with a Golden Egg, hearts, shamrocks and a pot of gold, a New Year countdown with fireworks and confetti, hidden stars, a Thanksgiving gratitude table, autumn leaves and an Earth Protector hunt.

Rewards are permanent: badges and Rex skins you can equip (your Home page Rex only changes when you pick one). Rewards are only given when the requirements are met, never twice, and stay after an event ends. Archived events keep your progress.

Effect Lab has 15 new seasonal styles (ghosts, bats, pumpkins, orange sparks, fireworks, eggs, shamrocks, flowers, summer sun, school, presents, nature, cozy autumn, paws, arcade). Live Events reuses the same effects, never changes your saved Effect Lab or theme settings, and respects reduced motion.

You can change an event's start and end dates on this device in Live Events > Settings, hide the collectibles, or turn event effects off. Live Events saves only to its own rexev1_ keys. Updating still only happens when you press Update Now.

history.summary: A small tidy-up: the shortcuts list now shows the newer shortcuts, and a few little fixes.

items.text: The keyboard shortcuts list (press ?) did not mention Quick note (Alt+N) or Focus sounds. It does now.
Pressing ? while a dropdown was focused, or while a Rex dialog (like Quick note) was open, could pop up the shortcuts list on top. It no longer does.
Between midnight and 5 AM the Home greeting says "Burning the midnight oil" instead of "Good morning".

history.summary: Focus sounds: calm rain, brown noise, white noise and wind for working, with a volume slider and a sleep timer.

items.text: Focus sounds on the Dev Clock page: Rain, Brown noise, White noise or Wind, with a volume slider and an optional stop timer (15 min, 30 min, 1 hour). The sound is generated in your browser, so there are no files to download and it works offline.

Nothing ever plays by itself. Press a sound to start it, press it again (or Stop) to end it. "Toggle focus sound" is also in the command palette (Ctrl/⌘+K). Your last sound, volume and timer are remembered.

history.summary: Quick notes from anywhere (Alt+N), and Rex's day now shows your week and your streak.

items.text: Quick Capture: press Alt+N (Option+N on a Mac) anywhere, use "Quick note" in the command palette (Ctrl/⌘+K), or the Quick note button on Home. Type a note and press Ctrl/⌘+Enter. It is saved into the Knowledge Base list, so it appears on that page with its category and tags.
Rex's day now shows a 7-day focus chart (hover a bar for that day) and a streak counter for consecutive days with Dev Clock time or sent messages. An unfinished today does not break your streak.

history.summary: New on Home: "Rex's day", a card where Rex's mood follows what you really did today.

items.text: Home now shows Rex's day: Rex is sleepy, awake, happy or on fire depending on your Dev Clock focus time and the messages you sent today, with a progress bar toward your daily focus goal, your open tasks, and a Pet Rex button that counts your pets.

Home "Webhooks sent today" and the daily counters used the UTC date, so in the evening (after about 8 PM in US Eastern time) they rolled over to "tomorrow" early. They now use your own local day. Older daily totals are kept.
The card only reads data already stored in this browser (Dev Clock, sent history, tasks). It adds no new account, server or storage except a small pet counter.

history.summary: The Update Center page is gone. Everything it did now lives in Settings, App & Updates, plus a few bug fixes.

items.text: Removed the Update Center page and its sidebar item. Check for Updates, Auto Check, Update Now, release notes, Go back and Repair are all in Settings, App & Updates. Updates are still never installed by a refresh or by checking.
The "Update notifications" switch in Settings did nothing. When a check finds a new version, Rex now adds one notification (once per version) if that switch is on.
Exported backups were always named "project-rex-v42-backup.json". The file name now includes the real version.
The "Check for Updates" command and the red update dot now open Settings, App & Updates instead of a page that no longer exists.

history.summary: Refreshing or reopening Rex no longer installs updates. Updates are now a button you press, from a brand-new Update Center, and Settings is reorganised.

items.text: Refreshing, reopening or relaunching Rex no longer installs a new version by accident. Rex now runs from a saved copy of the version you installed, and only the Update now button (after a confirmation) can change it. Your settings, profile, projects, webhooks and backups are never touched by a refresh.

New Update Center page: running version, latest published version, status, last successful check, Check for Updates, Auto Check, Update Settings, Update Now, the latest release card, and a Release History table (cards on phones).
Checking, finding and installing are now three separate steps. Check for Updates and Auto Check only look; nothing is installed until you confirm Update Now. Auto Check can be turned off.

Safer installs: Rex downloads the whole new version first, checks every file against a fingerprint, and only then switches. If anything fails the old version keeps running and an error explains what happened. Go back and Repair also live in Update Settings.

Update Log: the "Current release" label used the first list entry instead of the version that is really running, and the published history was cut off at 25 releases. Labels now compare running, latest and installed correctly, the log is sorted and de-duplicated, and the full history is published.
Settings rebuilt: a search box, clearer groups, a "Saved" confirmation on every change, update preferences, and confirmations on destructive actions. Resetting all data now asks you to type RESET.

Reset all data could quietly bring your data back: Rex saved itself again while the page was closing. Reset now really erases, after saving a restore point (and it stops if that restore point cannot be saved).
When Discord's image server could not be reached, the default avatar retried itself endlessly (hundreds of failed requests per second). It now falls back once to a local placeholder.
Safer sharing: a new "Export without webhook URLs" button and a "Copy diagnostics" button that remove Discord webhook secrets before anything is shared.
The red update dot now shows how many updates are waiting (for example 3) on the menu button, the More tab, Settings, the page title, and the installed app icon.
Update history: Settings, App & Updates now keeps a list of every update you installed, with the date, how long it took, and how many updates were installed in one go.

Dev Clock: on phones the Today, This week, Streak, All time and Average cards were wider than the screen, so the whole page could be dragged sideways. The timer and the stat cards now stack in one column on phones and small tablets.
Command palette: "Check for Updates" crashed with an error because it opened a page that no longer exists. It now opens Settings, App & Updates, and checks right away.
The old update-check function no longer errors if its page elements are missing; it hands over to the new Updates card instead.

Skip ahead: if you missed more than one update, Rex lists every update you are behind and what each one added. One Install all button jumps straight to the newest and installs all of them, so you never have to update one at a time.
The update screen and the What's new card now show every version you caught up on, grouped by version number.
The website's version.json is now built automatically from the Update Log, so release notes are written once.
The update waiting screen is now something to look at: a drifting aurora background, a glowing progress ring around the Rex logo, a live checklist of each step, and rotating What's new and tip cards.
Catch the bones: a tiny game on the update screen. Tap the falling bones (stars are worth 5) while you wait. Your best score is saved.
The red update dot now stays on the menu button, More tab, and Settings after you leave the page, and is repainted on every page change.
Rex now checks for updates by itself: when you open it, every 10 minutes, when you come back to the app, and when your phone gets back online, so the dot shows up without pressing anything.
When an update is waiting, the browser tab title shows a dot and an installed app icon shows a badge where the device supports it.
Big and small updates: a big release (new features) shows the full-screen update for about 3 minutes, and a small fix shows it for about 1 minute.
Go back: Rex keeps a copy of your previous version. If an update breaks something, Settings, App & Updates, Go back switches to it, and Update now returns to the newest. Your data is not touched.
Update notification dots: a pulsing red dot shows on the menu button, the More tab, and Settings while an update is waiting.
The update screen keeps your phone awake while it runs, and the stage messages and time remaining now cover the longer wait.

New full-screen update experience: a black screen with the Rex logo, a thin progress bar, stage messages, time remaining, and the expected finish time. It lasts about 22 seconds, then restarts Rex and shows What's new.
The update screen now shows the time now, how long it has taken, and when it should finish, plus a What's new list for the version you are installing.
After an update finishes, Rex shows a "Rex is now vX" card with what changed and how long the update took.
Update button now shows a progress screen with a percentage, the file being downloaded, and about how many seconds are left, then confirms when the update is complete.
Phone buttons felt finicky because touchscreens kept a sticky hover state and a tap delay. Hover effects are now off on touch devices, taps respond instantly, and buttons and tabs are larger.

Update button: Settings, App & Updates, now has Check for updates. When a newer version is on the website, Rex shows what is new and an Update now button that reloads with the newest files so you never need a hard refresh. Rex also checks quietly when it opens. Your data is not touched.
Phone layout rebuilt: the squeezed icon rail is gone. On phones Rex now has a slim top bar, a slide-out menu with full names, and a bottom tab bar (Home, Webhooks, Holidays, Clock, More).
Settings redesigned into sections (Appearance, General, Alerts, Weather, Data, App & Updates) with clean rows, bigger touch targets, and a stacked layout on phones.
New app icon: a drawn Rex dog face replaces the emoji for the installed app, home screen, and browser tab, and the sidebar logo.
The offline service worker now asks the server for the newest copy of each file, so updates show up faster after a release.

Rex Backup: automatic daily backups kept in this browser (newest 5, skipped when nothing changed), a one-click Download backup file button, Restore from a file, a status badge that shows whether your data is really protected, and an optional reminder to download a file every 7, 14, or 30 days.

Achievements: a new page with 16 achievements and Bronze, Silver, and Gold tiers that unlock from what you really do in Rex (messages sent, Dev Clock hours and streaks, favorited holidays, projects, tasks, notes, backups, friends, and more). Includes progress bars, unlock dates, a Rex rank, and a toast when you unlock something.

Pomodoro mode on the Dev Clock page: focus, short break, and long break phases with a progress ring, Start/Pause/Skip/Reset, session dots, optional auto-start, sound and desktop notifications, the time in the browser tab title, and a weekly summary chart. Timer settings are adjustable and the timer keeps running when you change pages.

Install Rex as an app: Rex now has an app icon, works offline, and shows an Install button in Settings (on the hosted website) so it can open in its own window from your desktop, dock, or home screen.

Restore points used to save a copy of every earlier restore point inside each new one, which made backups grow very large. New snapshots no longer do this, and older ones are cleaned up automatically.
Saving a restore point now shows a clear message when browser storage is full instead of failing silently.
The Version Rollback page is now called Rex Backup and sits on the new backup dashboard.
Holiday Center: the calendar was far too tall because its day cells were forced to 62px. Day cells are now compact, which shortens the calendar by about 125px.

The next-holiday spotlight card was too big because it stretched to the calendar height. It is now compact, and on wide screens the Upcoming Holidays list sits under it with the calendar on the right. On smaller screens everything stacks.
Holiday Center: tap ☆ on any holiday to add it to your favorites, then use the new ⭐ Favorites filter to see only those.
Holiday Center: add a holiday to your phone or computer calendar with the new 📅 button, or use Export .ics to download the next 12 months of holidays in one file.
Custom holidays can now be edited in place (✏️ on the list or Edit in Saved Holidays) instead of deleted and re-added.
The Upcoming Holidays list no longer stops at 14 rows; use Show more to keep going, and search now looks across the full upcoming list.
Added a Current Update card to the Home page that shows the installed version and opens the Update Log when clicked.
Aligned the page title, sidebar, status line, About card, Home card, and app version constant so they all report the same version.
Fixed the holiday ⓘ button breaking on descriptions that contain apostrophes (for example Mother's Day or Veterans Day).
Friend names, status text, avatars, and custom ping labels are now escaped before display, so a shared profile code can no longer inject HTML.
Restore points now record the real app version, and the LATEST tag in the Update Log is applied automatically to the newest release.
Added the missing V10.3.1 release to the history and prepared the project for GitHub and GitHub Pages.
Fixed the Update Log header and current-release badge, which were stuck displaying V10.2.0 even when newer releases were included.
The Update Log now synchronizes its visible version labels and latest-release panel from the release history each time it renders.
Added a Refresh Log control and an initial render fallback so the release timeline can be rebuilt without leaving the page.
Rebuilt Edit Profile with a responsive layout, clearer live preview, and a sticky save bar on larger screens.
Added a live profile-completion meter, random/clear avatar actions, banner reset, and copyable profile summary.
Limited profile links to 8 and validates http/https URLs before saving to prevent broken links.
Stopped the editor from inserting a fake current-project value when that field is blank.
Retained the previous Profile Center fixes for import validation, preferences, responsive cards, and compact mode.
Improved resilience for older or partial profile data and nested preferences.
Stronger validation for profile-only backups and safer settings import.
Profile export download timing now works more reliably in Safari.
Refined profile cards, responsive spacing, compact mode, focus states, and accent styling.
Expanded the Profile page with local profile personalization controls for accent color and compact card layout.
Added profile-only JSON export and import so profile details and preferences can be moved between browsers or computers.
Profile dashboard keeps existing bio, avatar, status, banner, links, badges, creator spotlight, and statistics.
Profile imports validate the backup format and confirm before replacing profile fields; project data and Project Notebook entries are not overwritten.
All profile preferences remain local to the browser; no account or cloud service is required.
Fixed Project Notebook discoverability by adding a dedicated Project Notebook page to the main sidebar, rather than requiring users to find the notebook inside individual project cards.
Added a project selector on the dedicated notebook page so users can choose a project and view or add its existing notebook entries.
Improved notebook page layout and small-screen form spacing while keeping notebook entries stored with their existing project data.
Updated app version labels and the Update Log to V10.2.0. This release is focused on bug fixes and usability corrections; no new feature areas are planned for this version.
Introduced Rex Studio, a project workspace with project cards, custom icons and cover-image URLs, searchable projects, pinned favorites, and Planning, In Progress, On Hold, and Complete statuses.
Added project task lists with completion checkboxes and automatic progress bars for each project.
Added Recent Activity to Rex Studio to track project creation, status changes, edits, pins, and task updates.
Added the Project Notebook so each project can keep its own notes, useful links, reference images, code snippets, and decisions together.
Added project-level notebook entries with categories, titles, content, optional URLs, and local browser storage.
Added Knowledge Base, Automation Lab, Task Center, System Monitor, and Restore Points as separate workspace areas.
Added local restore points with labeled snapshots, restore safety backups, and JSON backup import/export for saved browser data.
Clarified that restore points restore saved browser data and settings; reverting the actual app code requires opening an older app release.

Project Rex Center V10.0.0 major visual refresh: redesigned the sidebar navigation, workspace switcher, top bar, cards, statistics, form controls, and modal surfaces for a more cohesive command-center look.
Holiday Center Festive Edition: added a live overview with the next holiday, upcoming holidays this month, and your custom holiday count.
Added holiday search across names, categories, and descriptions while retaining the existing category filters and hidden-holiday controls.
Refined colorful Holiday Center cards, calendar highlights, theme previews, and mobile spacing while preserving existing holiday settings and bot controls.
Added a persistent save-status indicator in the top bar so you can see when your data is saved, when a save is in progress, or when saving fails.
Added clearer active navigation styling, a more structured content header, refined spacing, responsive navigation behavior, and reduced-motion accessibility support while preserving existing tools.

Expanded Profile with a Developer Snapshot for role, current project, favorite tools, and optional region/timezone, plus editable goals, skills being learned, and interests. These details save locally and are included in profile share codes.
Holiday Calendar now stays visible beside the upcoming-holiday spotlight, giving the main Holiday Center a compact, always-open calendar.
Added Effect Lab controls for custom falling symbols: use your own emoji, letter, or number, then adjust the effect and preview it on screen.
Custom holidays can use their own falling symbol as a seasonal screen effect, so a holiday can have a personal visual style.
Cleaned up the main Holiday Center spotlight card with tighter spacing and clearer actions so the next upcoming holiday stays the focus.
Expanded the Profile spotlight with a more prominent creator summary and a shortcut to update profile details.
Refreshed the Update Log with a release header, feature summaries, clearer search and filter controls, and more polished version cards.
Update Log cards now include a prominent illustrated-style release banner, a featured latest-release panel, and expandable details for each version.
Added per-release copy-link controls and a local “seen” marker so you can identify releases you have opened and share a specific update.
Fixed the featured latest-release banner so its colorful thumbnail background is visible instead of appearing as a blank white panel.
Added Update Achievements with collectible milestone badges that unlock from the recorded release history: First Feature Added, Bug Squasher, and Major Release.
Expanded release history with a “What’s New Since Last Visit” filter and dedicated release-detail views showing version, date, and categorized change notes.

Repaired the Holiday Calendar interactions: dates are selectable, selected-day details and holiday descriptions appear below the calendar, and greeting/countdown actions are available from each holiday.
Polished the Holiday Calendar with clearer month listings, selected-day highlighting, keyboard-accessible day buttons, and more readable responsive layouts.
Added expand/collapse controls for release notes, clearer release summaries, and responsive card layouts for smaller screens.
Aligned the app title, sidebar version, builder/about version labels, and Update Log with V10.0.0.
Added a periodic save safety net plus save attempts when the page is hidden or closed, helping capture changes even if a feature misses its normal save call.
Save failures are now reported more clearly instead of being silently ignored. Dev Clock storage errors are also caught so they do not crash the page.
Rewrote the built-in holiday descriptions in plain language for clearer, more useful explanations in the app.

Holidays now show a short description or tip when you hover over them, and each holiday row in the Upcoming list has a small “ⓘ” button that opens the same description in a popup. This makes it easier to see what each holiday is about before you send a greeting or set up a bot post.
Holiday descriptions are stored directly in the holiday definition, so they appear consistently on the Home banner, in the Holidays list, on the Calendar tooltips, and inside the Holiday Bot preview.

Holiday Bot now adds a 💡 fun fact under each post, like "Halloween started as the Celtic festival Samhain." There are 3 facts for each of 28 holidays, and they rotate by day so a long countdown doesn't repeat. Turn it off any time with the Fun fact line switch.

New Weekly Digest: once a week (Monday by default) the bot posts the next 3, 4, or 5 holidays with their dates and days left. Pick the day and how many holidays, and see a live preview in Holidays → Holiday Bot.
Added a "Digest didn't send — send it now" button, plus a digest status line (✅ sent at…, ⏳ scheduled for…, ⚠️ not sent yet). The Home warning and Send it now button also cover a missed digest.
Digests respect your ping, embed style, holiday-type filters, post time, and the Scheduling pause, and only send once per day.
The Update Log now shows the date and time of each update next to its version number, and the newest one is marked with a LATEST tag.
Updates from 9.5.1 through 9.5.5 now show their date. Older versions don't have a recorded date, so they still show only the version number.
Added an "It didn't send — send it now" button to Holiday Bot. If you notice the post never showed up in Discord, one tap sends today's message right away, even if Rex thinks it was already sent.

Holiday Bot now shows a Today's post status (✅ sent at…, ⏳ scheduled for…, or ⚠️ not sent yet), and Home shows a warning with a Send it now button when a post is late, paused, or was rejected by Discord.
Sending a holiday message by hand from Holiday Bot now counts as that day's post, so the bot no longer posts a duplicate later.
Holiday Bot posts now include a progress bar that fills up as the holiday gets closer, like ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░ — easy to read at a glance in Discord.
Holiday Bot now has a streak counter: "Day 7 of the Halloween countdown!", with a 🔥 every 7th day and "Countdown complete! 🎉" on the holiday itself. Works in daily countdown mode.
Both extras have their own on/off switch in Holidays → Holiday Bot, and the live preview shows exactly what the next message will look like.
Holiday Bot messages now start with @here by default, like "@here 🎃 Halloween is in 25 days!". You can still switch the ping to @everyone or no ping in Holidays → Holiday Bot → Ping.

New Holiday Bot (Holidays → Holiday Bot): automatically posts messages like "Halloween is in 25 days!" to a Discord webhook of your choice. It auto-picks a webhook with "holiday" in its name and turns itself on when it finds one.

Two modes: a daily countdown that starts a set number of days before the next holiday (default 30), or milestone posts only on chosen days (30, 14, 7, 3, 1 days before, or the day of). On the day itself it posts the holiday greeting.

Choose which holiday types it announces (US, Fun, Cultural, Custom), what time it posts, plain text or text with an embed card, and an optional @everyone / @here ping. Each message is only sent once, and if Rex opens after the post time it catches up.

Holiday Bot posts show up in History, Timeline, and the sent counters like any other webhook message, and a Send next holiday now button lets you test it instantly. Pausing Scheduling also pauses the bot.

New Holidays page (Tools → Holidays) with a live countdown to the next holiday, an upcoming list, and a month calendar. Covers US holidays, fun days (Pi Day, Star Wars Day, Programmers' Day, National Dog Day…), and cultural holidays (Lunar New Year, Diwali, Hanukkah, Easter, Cinco de Mayo).

Holiday Mode: during a holiday season Rex gets themed colors plus animated effects — falling snow at Christmas, bats and pumpkins at Halloween, fireworks on the 4th of July, rising hearts on Valentine's Day, falling leaves at Thanksgiving, and more. 22 themes total, and you can preview any of them from the Holidays page.
Home now has a next-holiday banner and a smarter greeting — it changes with the time of day, and wishes you a happy holiday on the day itself.

One-click holiday messages: ✉️ loads a themed greeting and ⏳ loads a "X days until…" countdown post straight into the Webhook Builder. Also added a 🎉 Holiday Greeting template to the Templates library.
Custom Holidays — add your own days (birthdays, launch dates, anniversaries) with an emoji, once or repeating every year. They show up in the list, calendar, banner, and notifications.
Notifications now remind you one week before and on the day of each holiday, once per holiday. On the day, Rex also throws a little confetti.

Tap Rex on the Home page for a confetti burst. Random Rex also gets holiday-themed quotes during a holiday season. The Command Palette gained Open Holidays, Compose Next Holiday Greeting, Toggle Holiday Effects, and Confetti.
Effects and colors can be switched off separately, with an amount slider. They pause automatically when your system or Appearance settings turn animations off, and individual holidays can be hidden.
Solemn days (Memorial Day, Veterans Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day) use a respectful mode — colors only, with no confetti or falling effects.
Timeline now has search and a type filter (Webhook, Testing, Template, Schedule, etc.), plus a Clear button — it was the only history-style page in Rex without them.
Timeline entries now show a colored icon per activity type instead of plain text, so it’s easy to scan at a glance.

Analytics’ "Template Usage" stat was guessing which templates you used by checking if the sent message text happened to contain the template’s name or title — a false-positive-prone hack. It now tracks real usage the moment you load a template into the builder.
Analytics now shows Testing Events, Active Events, and Total Testers alongside the webhook stats, and a top-5 breakdown of your most-used webhooks.
Added a custom color picker to the message Text Color toolbar — pick any color and it snaps to the closest of Discord’s 8 supported message colors, shown live in the preview.
Added real Discord text formatting — Bold, Italic, Underline, and Strikethrough buttons above the message box, using normal Discord markdown so it works on mobile too (unlike the color trick).
Live Preview now renders Bold/Italic/Underline/Strikethrough, not just colors, so what you see is much closer to what actually gets sent.
Cleaned up and shortened the helper text under the color and formatting tools so the Discord limitations are easier to understand at a glance.
Text color buttons now correctly restore your cursor position after inserting a color tag instead of jumping to the end of the message.
Added a Font Family picker in Settings → Appearance → Interface — choose Inter, Poppins, Roboto, Lexend, Merriweather, Fira Code, or your system font for the whole app.
Added a custom Text Color option in the same Interface tab, with swatches, a full color picker, and a one-tap reset back to the theme default.

Added a TEXT COLOR toolbar to the Message composer in Webhooks — select text and pick a color to send it in color on Discord desktop/web, using Discord’s ANSI code-block trick (Discord has no real custom-font support for messages, so font choice only applies to Rex’s own interface, not the sent message).
The Live Preview now renders ANSI text colors so you can see exactly how a colored message will look before sending.
Fixed several places (Webhook Builder, Appearance card, About page, Reset Appearance toast) that were still hard-coded to say "V6.0.0" instead of the actual running version.
Redesigned the Home page hero into a large gradient banner instead of a plain card.
Home's overview cards (Weather, Time, Next Event, Webhooks) now each have their own colorful gradient icon badge instead of a flat icon.
Quick Actions and info cards now lift and glow more distinctly on hover for a livelier feel.
Sidebar got a subtle shadow and slightly more breathing room to feel more like a distinct panel.
Full component refresh across the entire app: buttons, inputs, dropdowns, badges, and modals all redesigned with bolder rounded corners and the new purple/pink accent.
Inputs and textareas now show a soft glow ring when focused instead of a plain border.
Sidebar links glow with a colorful gradient when active, and gently highlight on hover.
Modals got bigger rounded corners and a softer, colorful shadow instead of plain black.
Notification tags, mention buttons, and small action buttons are now pill-shaped and bolder.
Added a custom colorful scrollbar that matches the new theme.
Removed Quiet Hours entirely — the settings card, notification tagging, and all related code are gone from Notifications.
Overhauled the entire visual design system into a vibrant, Govee Home-inspired look: purple-to-pink gradient accents, bright white cards with bolder rounded corners, and punchier shadows.
The active sidebar item and primary buttons now use a colorful gradient instead of flat blue, giving the app a livelier, more playful feel while keeping it clean and readable.
Dark mode was re-tuned to match the new purple/pink palette instead of the old blue theme.
Removed System Health entirely — the page, sidebar entry, and Diagnose modal are gone.
Fixed Escape not closing most modals — the Keyboard Shortcuts panel said Esc closes any open modal, but it only closed the command palette. It now closes any open modal.
Added a "Copy diagnosis" button in System Health's Diagnose modal, so you can paste the cause and fix straight into a support channel.
Added Quiet Hours to Notifications — set a time range where new notifications save silently in the background without bumping the badge or interrupting you.
Notifications that arrived during quiet hours are now tagged "🌙 quiet hours" in the list so you know what you missed.
Added a Keyboard Shortcuts panel — press ? anywhere or click the new ⌨️ header button to see every shortcut Rex supports.
Removed the "Simulate an issue" dropdown from System Health — the page now only ever shows real, live status.
Added a "Simulate an issue" dropdown on System Health so you can preview what a failure looks like — clearly labeled 🧪 SIMULATED so it's never mistaken for a real problem.
The health disclaimer now updates to say when a simulation is active, with a one-click "Clear simulation" link.
Added a "Diagnose" button to every System Health card and detail row — click it to see the likely cause and a suggested fix.
Added a System Health page — a live status board for Webhooks, Weather, Testing, Scheduler, Local Storage, and Dev Clock, all pulled from real app data.
Added an overall status indicator that turns yellow or red if any system needs attention.
Custom pings can now target a specific person, not just a role — pick "Person" and paste their Discord user ID.
Ping buttons now show a small icon (🏷️ role / 👤 person) so it's clear what each one pings.
Added a Share Profile code you can send to friends — they paste it into Add Friend to save your profile card locally, no server or account required.
Added a Friends list on the Profile page, with the ability to remove friends.
Added an emoji/icon picker for your avatar, as an alternative to pasting an image URL.
Profile name editing was already supported — Edit Profile now makes it clearer alongside the new icon picker.
Completely redesigned Profile page into a Discord-style developer profile with a banner, avatar, status, and bio.
Added custom status presets (Online, Busy, Do Not Disturb, Invisible) with editable status text.
Added banner styles: Solid, Gradient, Aurora, or a custom image URL.
Added automatic badges (Developer, Rex Member, Beta Tester, Event Tester) based on real activity, plus a manual Early User badge.
Added Rex Developer Stats — webhooks sent, tests participated, templates created, and Dev Clock time — pulled live from existing app data.
Added a Links section for GitHub, Discord, Roblox, YouTube, website, or custom links.
Added Privacy controls to show/hide stats, badges, links, and member-since date.
Added a live-updating preview inside the new Edit Profile modal.
Smoother, cooler UI — pages now fade and slide in when you switch views instead of snapping instantly.
Cards gently lift on hover with a soft glow border, making the app feel more interactive and alive.
Buttons now give a quick press animation for tactile feedback on every click.
Overall polish pass to make Project Rex feel less like a static dashboard and more like a real web app.
Rex Desktop: a full visual redesign of the app shell — grouped sidebar sections (Home, Workspace, Testing, Monitoring, Tools, System), glass/blur panels, and a refreshed light-blue accent system.
Reorganized navigation to feel like a real desktop app instead of a flat page list.
Added a profile shortcut to the top header alongside search, notifications, and theme toggle.
Refined shadows, borders, and corner radii across every card and panel for a more polished, consistent look.
Redesigned the Update Log into a searchable, filterable timeline with tagged entries.
Removed the Screen Recorder feature and its tab from the sidebar.
Added an Update Log page to track what's changed over time.
Added a free, local Screen Recorder — no account, no upload, no cost.
Added pause/resume, a live timer, and an optional microphone toggle to the recorder.
Turned the Clock feature into a full dedicated page instead of a popup.
Added a daily goal ring, streak counter, average session length, and best day stat.
Added a 7-day bar chart with hover tooltips and a deletable session log.
Introduced the first version of the Dev Clock: clock in/out, live timer, and session history.
Project Rex command center baseline: webhook builder, templates, testing events, scheduling, history, timeline, analytics, weather, and appearance settings.
